summary: The board logic is small: one top module (bwidow.vhd) that wires the 6502, two POKEYs, RAM/ROM and an AVG together with block address decoders and a counter-chain IRQ, plus a functional AVG. The glue is closer to the board than to MAME. The IRQ is a 3 kHz divider feeding a 4-bit counter that is cleared by the acknowledge strobe, writes are decoded in 64-byte blocks, and the POKEY PIN ports carry the B4/D4 switch banks. MAME uses a periodic timer and single-address handlers instead. The AVG, the board's main custom logic, follows neither source: it decodes opcodes directly without the microcode PROM and uses an invented accumulator and normalize line drawer, so the overall lean is only weak.

findings.signal: IRQ from counter chain cleared by ack strobe
findings.mame_ref: bwidow.cpp:bwidow (set_periodic_int irq0_line_assert at CLOCK_3KHZ/12) and irq_ack_w
findings.note: The 1.5 MHz enable feeds a 9-bit 3 kHz counter, which steps a 4-bit counter. IRQ is the AND of counter bits 3 and 2, and intack_l resets the counter, much like a 74161 chain. MAME fires an abstract periodic interrupt and clears the line in a handler.

findings.signal: Block address decoding of write strobes
findings.note: The strobes for EAROM write/control, interrupt ack, VGGO and VGRST compare A15..A6, so each one covers a 64-byte block as a decoder PROM or '138 would. MAME maps go_w, reset_w and irq_ack_w to single addresses (0x8840, 0x8880, 0x88c0).

The top module instantiates one block per physical part (CPU, two POKEYs, program RAM, EAROM, AVG). Board signals such as VGGO/VGRST/halted, CS_L/RW_L and the POKEY PIN inputs (SW_B4/SW_D4 switch banks) are wired as ports. MAME's read handlers that merge ports, such as spacduel_IN3_r, have no counterpart.

findings.signal: AVG opcode-decode state machine without the microcode PROM
findings.mame_ref: bwidow.cpp ROM_REGION avg:prom (MAME's avg_device runs from this PROM; device source not provided)
findings.note: The AVG decodes each 3-bit opcode straight into named states (FETCHINSLO, DRAWVECSHORT, PUSHPCFORJUMP...) with a 4-entry stack. That is a functional reimplementation, not the board's PROM-sequenced state machine, and it also does not follow MAME's PROM-driven device, which also loads that PROM.

The drawer shifts dx/dy until their sign bits differ, then adds them into 26-bit position accumulators until a timer reaches the scale. This is a digital stand-in for the analog integrators and DAC timing, and it matches neither the board's circuit nor a MAME function.

Scale is computed as (256 - linear) shifted by the binary scale, and intensity is selected as 'intensity when mod=001 else mod<<5'. Any correct emulation has to produce these opcode semantics. The only link to MAME for the intensity line is a comment, so it is not counted as evidence.

findings.signal: CPU memory map and 3 kHz status bit
findings.note: The memory map regions match MAME's map, and latchin_c(7)=cnt_3khz(8) is bit 8 of the CPU cycle count, the same bit MAME's clock_r returns (total_cycles & 0x100). Core and emulator both have to share this.
The EAROM returns 0xFF and implements neither the ER2055 protocol nor MAME's earom_control_w bit mapping, so it gives no evidence either way.
The frame-rate throttle on the halted bit, the persistence gate and the DDR framebuffer rasterizer are FPGA display engineering and are not counted.
